title: Will you be as gods? Gaze in your omphalos. Hello! Kinch here. Put me on to Edenville.
html_source:
This line shifts greatly in language, but has a consistent theme, that of Dedalus' navel, and its relation to his birth and his own psyche. Let’s take this piece by piece:

Will you be as gods?

is in reference to Genesis 3:5,

For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

relating to Adam and Eve. Then,

Gaze in your omphalos

Omphalos = navel, there was a major conflict in theology over the ages over Adam and Eve’s navels (also known as the Omphalos hypothesis), and whether they should be there or not, and this in turn connects with the sudden shift in tone, from Biblical high style, to that of a conversation between a telephone operator and a caller,

Hello! Kinch here. Put me on to Edenville.

which in turn connects with the Adam and Eve references in the previous sentences.

Whew!
